item.text:
**8B.3 Research Note**
Bottom line: Kishida did mobilize the Japanese state fairly effectively in 2024, especially through the cabinet, Diet agenda, budget, expert panels, disaster response, security policy, and coalition bargaining. The main weakness is that this mobilization was politically fragile: the funding scandal, low approval, and factional compromise narrowed his room to maneuver.

**Positive**
- [Policy Speech by Prime Minister Kishida to the 213th Session of the Diet](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202401/30shiseihoshin.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024-01-30 | Kishida explicitly asked the Diet to turn the year’s priorities into concrete action, tying the agenda to wage growth, child support, disaster response, fiscal reform, digital administration, labor reform, and defense buildup. This is direct evidence of mobilizing the cabinet and bureaucracy toward the chosen program. | QIDs: 8B.1, 8B.2, 8B.3
- [Press Conference by Prime Minister Kishida](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202406/21kaiken.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024-06-21 | Kishida said the reform headquarters had pushed core political-funding measures, the law had been amended, and the next steps were a third-party inspections-and-audits body plus lower disclosure thresholds. That shows actual institutional mobilization, not just rhetoric. | QIDs: 8B.2, 8B.3
- [Liaison Meeting of the Government and Ruling Parties](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/actions/202407/03sei_yoto.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024-07-03 | Kishida reported that nearly all bills and treaties passed, including the Political Funds Control Act, child-care support, and food/agriculture legislation, and he credited the government-ruling-party coalition. This is strong evidence of effective coalition mobilization through the Diet. | QIDs: 8B.2, 8B.3
- [Expert Panel toward Improving Response Capabilities in the Field of Cybersecurity](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/actions/202406/07cyber.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024-06-07 | Kishida convened a 17-expert panel and ordered ministers to turn its results into bills as early as possible. This is a concrete example of mobilizing the bureaucracy and expert apparatus toward the security program. | QIDs: 8B.2, 8B.3
- [Japan government agrees to measures to help restart Tepco’s nuclear reactor](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/TOKYO-ELECTRIC-POWER-COMP-6491247/news/Japan-government-agrees-to-measures-to-help-restart-Tepco-s-nuclear-reactor-47818629/) | Reuters | 2024-09-06 | Reuters reported the government agreed to reinforce evacuation measures and secure local consent for a reactor restart. This shows practical mobilization of regulators, local authorities, and safety planning for a policy objective. | QIDs: 8B.2, 8B.3
- [Statement by Prime Minister KISHIDA Fumio upon the General Resignation of the Kishida Cabinet](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202410/1001danwa.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024-10-01 | Kishida summarized his term as economic revival, defense strengthening, and political reform, and said the cabinet had worked to restore accountability after the fundraising scandal. That reflects an intentional attempt to mobilize the cabinet and party around a defined program, even at the end of the term. | QIDs: 8B.1, 8B.3
- [Kishida’s legacy: Scandals and compromise at home, global respect for security and diplomacy](https://www.ksat.com/news/world/2024/09/30/kishidas-legacy-scandals-and-compromise-at-home-global-respect-for-security-and-diplomacy/) | Associated Press | 2024-09-30 | AP said Kishida improved ties with South Korea, deepened cooperation with the United States and other partners, and won respect abroad for his defense and security posture. This supports the view that he effectively mobilized alliance networks toward his chosen strategic direction. | QIDs: 8B.3

**Negative / Mixed**
- [Embattled Japan PM faces ethics committee, with popularity and budget on the line](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/embattled-japan-pm-faces-ethics-committee-to-save-popularity-and-budget-3319362) | Reuters | 2024-02-28 | Reuters described Kishida as the first sitting Japanese PM to appear before a parliamentary ethics committee, with the scandal threatening his popularity and the budget process. This shows mobilization was constrained by defensive crisis management, not just directed upward and outward. | QIDs: 8B.3, 7B.9
- [Japan's lower house passes budget in win for PM Kishida](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/japans-lower-house-passes-budget-in-win-for-pm-kishida-3319362) | Reuters | 2024-03-02 | The budget passed in a rare Saturday session, but Reuters framed it as a win for a leader whose public support had slumped. That is evidence of institutional success, but also of fragile political capital behind the mobilization. | QIDs: 8B.2, 8B.3
- [Kishida’s legacy: Scandals and compromise at home, global respect for security and diplomacy](https://kyma.com/news/2024/09/30/kishidas-legacy-scandals-and-compromise-at-home-global-respect-for-security-and-diplomacy/) | Associated Press | 2024-09-30 | AP said Kishida was seen at home as a leader who compromised with powerful conservative nationalists to stay in power. That is mixed evidence: coalition bargaining helped him mobilize power, but it also indicates dependence on bloc management rather than purely programmatic control. | QIDs: 8B.3, 8B.1
- [Japan’s PM says LDP race should be transparent and he will step aside](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202408/14kaiken.html) | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024-08-14 | Kishida’s own exit statement shows he chose transparent succession and withdrawal rather than attempting to retain office. This is not negative in a democratic sense, but it does mark the limits of his personal mobilization power by late 2024. | QIDs: 8B.3, 8B.1

**Search Gap**
- I found strong evidence that Kishida could mobilize formal institutions, budgets, expert panels, the Diet, and alliance/security channels.
- I did not find equally strong evidence of deep personal control over appointments or a disciplined loyalist machine; most mobilization appears institutional and coalition-based.
- The clearest negative evidence is political fragility: scandal, low approval, and compromise with conservative blocs, not a total failure to mobilize the state.
